newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI shares tipped to be sold in two issues.
newsitem.headline: ICI shares tipped to be sold in two issues.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc is likely to sell its 62.4 percent stake in ICI Australia Ltd in two tranches to minimise the price discount it will receive for the shares, an adviser on the sale said on Wednesday.
ICI Australia's shares are set to fall on ICI's announcement it would sell its stake to help it purchase Unilever Plc/NV's speciality chemicals business for US$8 billion.
The news came after ICI Australia's shares closed on Wednesday on the Australian Stock Exchange at A$12.44, valuing the parent company's 185 million share stake at A$2.301 billion.
"I think A$2 billion worth is a bit big for one tranche," said Tim Burroughs of Centaurus Corporate Finance, which is advising ICI Australia on the sell-down process.
"They (ICI Plc) have a pretty strong financial imperative to get some money in quickly but equally ... if they are seen as a forced seller, they will get screwed," he added.
The shares will be marketed to institutions in Australia, Europe, the United States and Asia. They are likely to be priced using a strike price rather than a fixed price, Burroughs said.
But the price is likely to be a substantial discount to the current market price, he told Reuters.
The first and bigger tranche is likely to be offered in the September quarter, and the remaining shares next year, he said.
"What you will see tomorrow is that the stock will open well down, then I think they will have to take a discount to that price (in the sale)," Burroughs said on Wednesday night.
ICI Australia managing director Warren Haynes told Reuters on Wednesday it would strive to retain its ties with ICI Plc but hinted the Australian firm would now broaden its horizons.
ICI Australia has been careful not to compete with its global parent in overseas markets.
"We will be able now to move into areas and geographic positions with possibilities we hadn't perhaps looked at before," Haynes said.
But it would be largely "business as usual" for ICI Australia, he said.
"Clearly at some stage in the future we will have to change our name," Haynes added.
